title: fix(plugin-sharing, runtime): a shared conversation's messages open for exactly the callers its share link opens for, on both mounts
body:
Fixes #23371
Clause-②: no — `/messages` now reaches the answer `/resolve` already gives the same caller for the same link, on the same mount; who can open a share link is unchanged.

## What changes

The share-link token door has two public routes. `/resolve` returns the shared record, and `/messages` returns a shared conversation's messages. Each route has two mounts: plugin-sharing's `registerShareLinkRoutes` and the runtime dispatcher's share-links domain. Both routes check the link through `IShareLinkService.resolveToken`, and its audience gate judges the inputs the route hands it. `/resolve` hands it the signed-in user, the recipient email and the password. `/messages` handed it fewer:

| Audience input | plugin-sharing `/messages` | dispatcher twin `/messages` |
|:--|:--|:--|
| the signed-in user (`signed_in` audience) | not passed, now passed | passed (unchanged) |
| the recipient email (`email` audience) | not passed, now passed | not passed, now passed |

Both `/messages` serves now read the two inputs from the same sources their own mount's `/resolve` reads. The signed-in user comes from the caller context the mount already resolved: the family door's `contextFromRequest` on the plugin mount, and the dispatcher's execution context on the twin. The session is not read a second time. The recipient email comes from `?email=`.

The landing points are the two `/messages` call sites, as dispatched. `/resolve`, `resolveToken` and `share-link-service.ts` are unchanged.

## Before and after

Measured in-process through both mounts' production handlers on SqlDriver: one engine, and one `ShareLinkService` with the production password hasher. "Opens" means `/messages` answers 200 with the conversation's messages. Every `/messages` refusal is `404 NOT_FOUND`.

| Link audience | Caller | `/messages` before (plugin / twin) | `/messages` after (both mounts) | `/resolve` (both mounts, unchanged) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `signed_in` | signed in | 404 / opens | opens | opens |
| `signed_in` | anonymous | 404 / 404 | 404 | `401 SIGN_IN_REQUIRED` |
| `email` | allowlisted email, signed in or not | 404 / 404 | opens | opens |
| `email` | no email or an off-list email, signed in or not | 404 / 404 | 404 | `404 INVALID_OR_EXPIRED` |
| `public`, `link_only` | anyone | opens / opens | opens | opens |

A password-protected link still needs its password on both routes; the inputs combine with the password `/messages` already passed.

## The boundary this keeps

After the fix, `/messages` opens for a caller exactly when `/resolve` on the same mount opens the same link for that caller with the same inputs. This was read off `resolveToken`, not assumed:

- Its verdict is binary: a result or `null`. The probe inputs feed only its audience and password gates. Every other gate reads the row, the object's policy and the record.
- The redaction set `/resolve` applies is the object default plus the link's own `redact_fields`, and no probe input reaches it. So `/resolve` serves no caller-specific reduced view. There is no cell where admitting a caller to `/messages` gives that caller more than `/resolve` gives it.
- `/messages` already returned the messages to `public` and `link_only` callers. The fix extends that to exactly the `signed_in` and `email` callers that `/resolve` already serves.

## The pin

`packages/runtime/src/domains/share-links-messages-audience.test.ts` has 85 cases.

- **One table of 28 requests.** It covers every caller and email combination for `signed_in` and `email`, the password combined with each of them, and `public` and `link_only` controls. It also carries the "it resolved" control: a link on an object that is not a conversation answers `/messages` with `400 UNSUPPORTED`, which `/messages` can only reach once `resolveToken` has passed.
- **Per mount, both routes.** Each row asserts `/messages`'s answer (the messages, `400 UNSUPPORTED` or `404 NOT_FOUND`, as `status` plus `error.code`). It also asserts `/resolve`'s answer to the same request (`status` plus `error.code`), so the two routes are held to one verdict per row.
- **Across mounts.** For each row, the two mounts' `/messages` answers are asserted equal on status, success flag, error code and payload.
- **Every declared audience.** The table's audience list is typed against `ShareLinkAudience` from the contract. An audience added there turns this file's typecheck red until it has rows. Checked once: with `email` taken out of the list, `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json` reports TS2322 at the assertion.

## Ablation (one-shot proof; no permanent test file)

Each leg mutates through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`: the anchor hits once, the blob changes, and the file is restored to its HEAD blob with `git diff HEAD` empty. The leg then rebuilds `@objectstack/plugin-sharing`, because the runtime suite reads its `dist/`. `scripts/ablation-dist-preflight.mjs` proves the marker is in `dist/`, and on the restore leg that it is absent with the tree clean. Only then does the file run.

| Leg | Mutation | Result |
|---|---|---|
| before | both `/messages` forwardings reverted: the plugin mount's signed-in user and email, and the twin's email | 18 failed, 67 passed. Exactly the enumeration's three "not forwarded" cells: plugin `signed_in` signed in (5 rows), plugin `email` allowlisted (4), twin `email` allowlisted (4), and the cross-mount `signed_in` rows (5) |
| negative 1 | `resolveToken`'s `signed_in` guard no longer refuses an anonymous caller | 10 failed: every anonymous `signed_in` row on both mounts. `/messages` answered 200, or 400 UNSUPPORTED, where the pin expects `404 NOT_FOUND` |
| negative 2 | `resolveToken`'s email allowlist check passes every caller | 12 failed: every no-email and off-list `email` row on both mounts, in the same shape |
| negative 3 | the twin's `/messages` hands an anonymous caller to `resolveToken` as a user (an over-forwarding) | 10 failed: the twin's anonymous `signed_in` rows, plus the cross-mount equality on each of them |
| restore | HEAD rebuilt, marker absent from `dist/`, tree clean | 85 passed |

## Tests

- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/runtime exec vitest run --project local src/domains/share-links-messages-audience.test.ts`: 85 passed.
- After merging `origin/main`, at `31350086ca`: runtime `src/domains/share-links*` plus `domain-floor-anonymous-deny.test.ts` gave 7 files and 291 tests passed. plugin-sharing `src/share-link*` gave 12 files and 271 tests passed.
- At `c127cb805`, before that merge (the merge brought only a `metadata-protocol` change and an `objectql` test):
  - `@objectstack/runtime` `vitest run --project local`: 382 files, 5717 passed, 19 skipped.
  - `@objectstack/plugin-sharing` `pnpm test`: 46 files, 1061 passed.
  - `pnpm typecheck` for both packages exits 0. The runtime test layer compiles the new file (confirmed with `--listFilesOnly`), and `check:test-typecheck` reports OK with the debt ledger unchanged.
- The runtime package's second vitest project, `repo` (the tests listed in `vitest.repo-tests.json`), was not run locally; it is declared to CI.

## Gates

Derived with `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` at `31350086ca`: 68 commands. All 68 were run on that head, each exit code captured before any pipe, and every one exits 0. `pnpm check:i18n` and `pnpm check:dual-build-cjs-loads` first answered `exit 3 PREREQUISITE NOT MET`. They were re-run after the prerequisite builds, which the gates themselves name: `check:i18n` reports "OK (10 package(s) — all bundles in sync)", and `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` exits 0. The `--ran` reconciliation reads "68 derived, 68 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN", with a derived zero because all 68 recorded an exit code. The full farm is CI's.

## Acceptance notes

- `/messages` returns `ai_messages` rows without applying the link's `redactFields`, which name the conversation's own fields. That was already so for `public` and `link_only` links, and it is unchanged here. No contract states that redaction applies to the related messages. Noted, not filed. Carrier: none.
- The console's shared-record page (objectui `SharedRecordPage`) reads any non-OK `/messages` answer as an empty list and shows "This conversation has no messages yet." After this fix, `/messages` refuses only the callers `/resolve` refused. The page now reaches that path only if the link is revoked or expires between its two calls. Noted, not filed. Carrier: none.
- On each mount, `/resolve` and `/messages` still each spell the audience inputs inline. One shared probe builder per mount would make a third audience input impossible to forget, but it touches `/resolve`, which is outside this card's surface. The pin above holds the class until then. Carrier: none.
- Refusal bodies differ between the mounts by one field: the twin's `error` also carries `httpStatus`. The pin compares status, flag, code and payload, not whole bodies. Pre-existing on every twin refusal; untouched here. Noted, not filed. Carrier: none.
